Order 
The appellants/claimants have filed this appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 being aggrieved by award dated 23.10.2024 passed in Claim Case No.171/2019 by the 2nd Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Manawar, District Dhar (M.P.), whereby a total compensation amount of Rs.15,63,400/- has been awarded in favour of the claimants.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.
3. Brief facts of the case are that on 22.04.2019, at about 3.30 PM, when the deceased Mukam @
Mukesh alongwith his relative Jitendra were going from Bedwalya to Vedla on motorcycle, at Singhana-Manawar main road, between Village Singhana and Borud, in front of a gas agency, at the same time, suddenly NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:12190 2 MA-166-2025 the offending motorcycle bearing registration No.MP11-MX-3109, which was being driven by respondent No.1 rashly and negligently dashed the motorcycle of the deceased from back, due to which he suffered grievous injuries on his head and other parts of the body and due to the said injuries, he died on his way to the hospital.
In the said accident, Jitendra also sustained grievous injuries on different parts of his body making him permanently disabled.
4. The dependents of the deceased filed a claim petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation.

5. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants contends that the compensation as awarded by the Claims Tribunal accepting earning of deceased as Rs.6,500/- per month was inadequate looking to the fact that he was working as skilled labourer and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
He also submits that income of deceased assessed by the Claims Tribunal is not just and proper.
Learned counsel for the appellants further submits that the compensation awarded by Claims Tribunal is on the lower side, therefore, the claimants seek enhancement of compensation.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation amount after assessing the income of deceased, which does not call for any interference by this Court.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8 .

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:12190 3 MA-166-2025 claimants.
So far as income of the deceased is concerned, as per the evidence that came on record, he is skilled labourer, therefore, his income should be assessed as Rs.7,700/- per month.
Therefore, his monthly income is fixed as Rs.7,700/- per month instead of Rs.6,500/- per month, as assessed by the Claims Tribunal.

Keeping in view the verdict of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 , the respective claimants are entitled for compensation under the head of future prospects @ 40% and compensation under other conventional heads.

Thus, the compensation awarded by Claims Claims Tribunal is modified as under:-
 Heads Amount  Income Rs.15,52,320/-
 (7700 + 40%(F.P.) X 12 X 16 (M) X 1/4)
 Consortium Rs.2,20,000/-
 Funeral Rs.16,500/-
 Loss of estate Rs.16,500/-
9 . Learned Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs. 15,63,400/-.

Thus, the appellants/claimants are held entitled to receive enhanced amount of Rs.2,41,920/- in addition to the amount of compensation already awarded by the Claims Tribunal, making the total compensation amount of Rs.18,05,320/-.
10.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
11. Rest of the conditions, as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

Thereafter, Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
13. Appeal stands allowed to the aforesaid extent and disposed of .
